errors.text_span: Основната цел е да се визуализира тенденцията на растежа на приходите и да се покаже процентното увеличение от година към година.
errors.evidence: The prompt asks the model to describe what the chart illustrates, not to infer its main purpose ('Основната цел е...'). This is a minor interpretation beyond a direct description.

errors.text_span: Оста Y представлява стойностите на приходите (в трлн. долара) и ръста (в проценти), като се използва една и съща ос, но с два различни типа данни.
errors.evidence: The Y-axis scale (0.00 to 25.00) corresponds only to the revenue in trillion dollars. The growth percentages are data labels placed on the line and do not correspond to the Y-axis scale.
The figure contains one area chart (the blue filled area representing 'Обобщени данни') and one line chart (the orange line for 'Ръст'), not two line charts.

errors.text_span: Синя линия, представляваща „Обобщени данни (в трлн. долара)“.
errors.evidence: The blue element is an area chart (a filled area), not a line. While it has a line as its upper boundary, its primary visual characteristic is the filled area.

errors.text_span: с по-голям наклон в началото и по-малък в края
errors.evidence: The description incorrectly states that the slope is greater at the beginning. In fact, the slope increases over time until 2022 (e.g., the jump from 2021 to 2022 is 3.10 trillion), and is smallest at the end (the jump from 2022 to 2023 is only 1.40 trillion).

errors.text_span: Тя е пунктирана, с оранжеви маркери (квадрати)
errors.evidence: The orange line in the chart is solid ('плътна'), not dotted/dashed ('пунктирана'). Also, there are no visible markers on the line itself; the square marker is only present in the legend.
The 14% growth value is associated with the year 2018 (representing the growth from 2017 to 2018). There is no growth value shown for 2017.

The description incorrectly assigns the growth percentages to the wrong years. The correct mapping is 14% for 2018, 13% for 2019, 15% for 2020, 16% for 2021, 19% for 2022, and 7% for 2023. The description shifts the first four values by one year and incorrectly duplicates the 16% value.
